name: Maelstrom Gate

stars.name: Maelstrom A
stars.notes: A fierce young white star whose ultraviolet glare scours the inner system; nothing soft survives within ten AU of its light.

stars.name: Maelstrom B
stars.notes: A dim red dwarf in a tight sub-companion orbit; its flares paint the inner planets' nightsides with brief crimson tides.

stars.name: The Riptide
stars.notes: A stellar-mass black hole in a wide outer orbit, betrayed only by a thin accretion haze of captured debris and the lensing shoal it drags behind it.

planets.name: Seething Rock
planets.notes: A molten-skinned world skimming the white primary; its lava seas are visible from three AU out and its orbit is slowly being torqued by the companion's pull.

planets.name: Charcoal Shoal
planets.notes: A radiation-blackened rock used as a hull test range by the navy; every crater on it has a serial number.

planets.name: Cold Helm
planets.notes: An airless S-type world circling the red dwarf alone; its far side faces the Riptide's lensing shoal, and instruments there disagree about where the stars actually are.

planets.name: Whirlwake
planets.notes: A vast storm-banded giant with a cyclonic eye visible from across the system; the navy's gate relay hangs in its shadow for shielding.

planets.name: Frostspit
planets.notes: A wind-scoured ice world at the system's cold rim, half its surface stripped to bare rock by particle weather off the accretion haze.

anomalies.name: Riptide Lens
anomalies.location: outer system, near the black hole's orbit
anomalies.notes: A wandering lensing shoal trailing the black hole that smears background starfields into false harbors; ships that steer by the wrong image end up somewhere else entirely.

anomalies.name: The Shear Line
anomalies.notes: A narrow fold corridor where space creases against itself; transit through it shortens weeks of travel into hours, but exit points drift unpredictably with the system's tidal phase.

asteroid_belts.name: Breaker Line
asteroid_belts.notes: A violent belt churned by competing tidal pulls; rocks cross the navigation lanes constantly, and the navy sweeps it weekly without ever clearing it.

stations.name: Breakwater Beacon
stations.notes: A barely crewed naval relay marking the safe transit channel through the maelstrom; its twelve keepers rotate out every ninety days, some before.

faction_control.notes: No faction holds Maelstrom Gate; the navy claims the beacon and the lane, smugglers claim the Shear Line, and the black hole claims everything eventually.

history: The first survey probe reported impossible starfields and was written off as malfunctioning; the second probe was lost inside the Breaker Line, and the third confirmed the Riptide's existence from a very cautious distance.
Naval cartographers charted the Shear Line during the Straits conflicts and turned an uninhabitable curiosity into the fastest known shortcut between the Wash and the Expanse.

Within the past two years, exit points along the Shear Line have begun drifting further with each tidal cycle, and Breakwater Beacon has logged arrivals days earlier than their own departure logs claim.
description: Three masters rule this water. A blazing white star floods the inner system with hard light beside a small red companion; far out in the dark, a nine-solar-mass black hole drags its faint accretion haze and a shoal of bent starlight behind it like a wake. Five battered planets survive in between: two scorched inner rocks, a lonely world circling the dwarf, a colossal storm giant, and a stripped ice field at the rim.

Nobody lives here, yet nobody can afford to ignore it. The Shear Line fold cuts weeks off the run between the Meridian Wash and the Brineward Expanse, so navy relays mark the safe channel while smugglers ride the fold's edges and pray. Traffic is light but constant: patrol cutters, gate pilots, and the occasional survey ship threading a system where navigation is less a science than seamanship.

The mysteries compound like standing waves. The Lens shows harbors that do not exist, the Shear Line delivers ships ahead of their own schedules, and Cold Helm's instruments insist the constellations are rearranging themselves when observed from its dark side. Breakwater Beacon's keepers have started keeping private logs. Whatever the Gate is becoming, the tide tables no longer predict it, and the next arrival may come from somewhere no chart has named.
